title: The naive framing: "it just tracks your tasks"
text: People assume the productivity plugin just tracks your tasks for you. It doesn't. It runs your whole day, tasks, meetings, email, and notes together. So, what does it actually do? Every other

title: It picks you, not a domain
text: Plugin in the collection picks a domain, sales, legal, finance. It points outward deep into one field. The productivity plugin points inward at the day you actually work through. Same engine, opposite aim. It picks you.

title: Fluent in you
text: It doesn't make Claude an expert in something. It makes Claude fluent in you, how your day is structured, what you owe people, what's on fire right now. That's why most people install it first. Five moves mostly, track tasks,

title: Five moves, not five apps
text: Prep for meetings, triage email, stay aware of your schedule, synthesize your notes. Not five apps, five things Claude can now do inside the conversation you're already having. Task management

title: You talk, it organizes
text: Is the base. Tell Claude what you need to do in plain language and it structures it. Tell it what's urgent and it sequences your day. No forms, no fields. You talk, it organizes.

title: Scattered becomes summary
text: Note synthesis is the quiet one. Information scattered across conversations, documents, and meetings gets pulled into one coherent summary, the stuff you'd normally lose between tabs. One caution up front, this isn't a

title: The wrong guess: not a to-do app
text: New to-do app and it doesn't replace your calendar. It's connective tissue. It makes Claude better at helping you work the tools you already have. The

title: Zero setup
text: Productivity plugin works the second you install it. No accounts to link, no connectors to authorize. That's rare in this collection and it's why it's a safe first install.

title: Still useful, sharper connected
text: One optional add-on, your calendar. Without it, the plugin is still useful. It just can't see your time. Connect one, the standard three steps, and Claude crosses a line. Now it knows what's committed, what's free, and where your focus blocks can go.

title: Just ask your day
text: Picture the first move of the day, before the tabs, before the noise. You just ask what your day looks like. What's my day look like? I have a client call at 10:00 and a proposal due Friday. What should I prioritize? Plain speech, real constraints. If your calendar's

title: Three streams, one plan
text: Connected, Claude fuses three streams, your schedule, the priorities you just named, and tasks left over from earlier conversations into one actionable plan, not a to-do list, a plan for the day sequenced. Second workflow before a

title: Prep before the room
text: Meeting that matters, you ask Claude to prepare you. It pulls context from your files, past conversations, and general knowledge into a briefing. You walk in already knowing who they are, what they want, and what to raise.

title: Sort, draft, review
text: Third, the inbox. Point it at a wall of unread mail, and it sorts by urgency. What needs a reply today? What can wait? What to archive? And drafts the easy ones for you to approve. Careful processing collapses into quick review.

title: Capture, don't switch
text: And the small one that saves you daily, capture without breaking flow. Something comes up mid-task, you say, "Add a follow-up with Sarah, due Thursday." It's logged, and you never left what you were doing.

title: Your method, adopted
text: Tell Claude how you already work, and it adapts. It doesn't impose a method. Say you prioritize with an urgency versus importance matrix, and that's how it lays your options out. Your rule, not its default.

title: It compounds
text: And it compounds. The more Claude knows about your recurring commitments, ongoing projects, and working patterns, the more useful it gets. You don't front-load any of it. It accrues one conversation at a time.

title: Set once, remembered
text: The shortcut for that is global instructions, persistent context that applies to every session. Your role, your typical week, how you like information presented. Set it once, Claude remembers.

title: Underneath it all
text: Think in layers. Your domain plugins, sales, legal, whatever you run, sit on top. Productivity sits underneath all of them, holding the day together while they do the specialist work.

title: The base holds
text: You swap specialists in and out as the work changes, but the base holds session after session, carrying your tasks and context forward. In practice, it feels less like an app and more like a desk that's already tidy when you sit down.

title: The anchor returns: your operating system
text: Add it up, and you get the pitch in the title. One generalist under a few specialists doing the same five moves from the top of this reel. Task tracking, meeting prep, email triage, schedule awareness, note synthesis. Now running underneath everything else. That's the operating system.

title: Carry-out
text: The productivity plugin doesn't specialize in a domain, it specializes in you working the moment you install it and getting sharper the more it knows how you work. That's why it's the layer most people never turn off. Your turn.

title: Your turn
text: Paste this into Claude. I just installed the productivity plugin and I want it to run my day. Ask me what I spend most of my time on and where my time leaks. Ask how I already prioritize. Then draft me a morning briefing routine and a Friday weekly review routine around my real schedule and tell me the one thing to put in global instructions so you remember it every session. title: Outro
text: Order the productivity plugin, lay him in for bear.
